questions.prompt: You paid the wrong person. What is a safe first move?

options.explanationWrong: Contacting unknown people does not help and can lead to more pressure.

options.text: Note the transaction ID and take a screenshot

options.explanationWrong: Paying more is a classic trick. You would lose more money.
Keep your proof. A complaint needs the transaction details.

questions.explanationCorrect: Save proof first: the transaction ID and a screenshot. You will need them for every complaint.

questions.prompt: Where should you raise your first complaint?

options.text: In the payment app you used, then contact your bank
In a public post on social media
options.explanationWrong: That is not an official route and can expose your details.

options.text: Only to the person who got the money
options.explanationWrong: A stranger has no duty to help. Use the official routes.

options.text: Nowhere, wait for it to come back
options.explanationWrong: Waiting does not start any process. Act as soon as possible.

questions.explanationCorrect: Start with the complaint option in your payment app and contact your bank, as soon as possible.

questions.prompt: The app and bank have not solved it. What next?

options.explanationWrong: There is another official route you can try.

options.text: Escalate through the NPCI dispute redressal process
Pay a 'recovery agent' you found online
options.explanationWrong: Recovery agents found online are often scams.

options.text: Share your PIN with a helper
options.explanationWrong: Never share your PIN with anyone.

questions.explanationCorrect: NPCI has a dispute redressal process. Check the current steps on official channels.
